title: Modern Unmodifiable & Immutable Collections
summary: Master modern Java immutable collection factories (List.of, Set.of, Map.of, copyOf): contrast structural immutability with unmodifiable views and Arrays.asList, understand null-rejection policies, and examine compact memory layouts.

activities.title: Practical Context: Read-Only Lens vs Laser-Etched Diamond
activities.description: Why modern systems require structural immutability rather than fragile wrapper views.
activities.content:
Consider two ways to protect a blueprint in an engineering facility. In the first approach, you place a laminated plastic sheet over the blueprint. Technicians looking through the glass cannot draw on the blueprint directly, but if someone modifies the original paper underneath the sheet, everyone looking through the glass sees the alterations.

In the second approach, the blueprint is laser-etched into a solid block of synthetic diamond. It is physically impossible to alter, has no backing paper to tamper with, and occupies the minimum possible space.

`Collections.unmodifiableList(list)` is the laminated sheet: an unmodifiable wrapper view whose contents change if the backing collection is mutated. In contrast, `List.of()` and `List.copyOf()` are laser-etched diamond: true structurally immutable collections with zero external backing dependencies, guaranteed thread safety, and zero mutation susceptibility.

activities.title: Architecture of Modern Immutable Collections
activities.description: Comprehensive comparison of factory methods, view mechanics, null policies, and memory compaction.
activities.content:
### Formal Computer Science Definition
An immutable collection is an algebraic data structure whose state cannot be modified after instantiation. In the Java runtime, immutable collections instantiated via `of()` and `copyOf()` factories provide structural immutability, disallow `null` references, strictly reject duplicate keys or set elements at construction, and utilize compact field-based layouts to minimize heap footprint.

### Comparative Architectural Matrix

| Feature | `Arrays.asList(arr)` | `Collections.unmodifiableList(c)` | `List.of(...)` / `List.copyOf(c)` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mutability** | Fixed-size mutable (`set()` allowed, `add()`/`remove()` fail) | Read-only view (mutations fail, backing list can mutate) | **Truly Immutable** (all mutations throw `UnsupportedOperationException`) |
| **Backing Dependency** | Direct link to original array | Direct link to backing collection | Independent snapshot (zero backing dependency) |
| **Null Support** | Allowed | Allowed (if backing allows) | **Strictly Forbidden** (throws `NullPointerException`) |
| **Thread Safety** | Thread-unsafe if shared | Thread-unsafe if backing collection mutates | **Inherently Thread-Safe** |
| **Memory Footprint** | Object header + array ref | Wrapper object + backing collection overhead | Highly optimized (`List12` uses 2 fields; `ListN` uses 1 flat array) |

### Core Contracts and Behavioral Dimensions

```
                    Modern Immutable Collections (Java 9+)
                                      |
        +-----------------------------+-----------------------------+
        |                                                           |
Direct Construction                                         Defensive Snapshot
- List.of(e1, e2, ...)                                      - List.copyOf(collection)
- Set.of(e1, e2, ...)                                       - Set.copyOf(collection)
- Map.of(k1, v1, k2, v2, ...)                               - Map.copyOf(map)
- Map.ofEntries(entry(k, v), ...)
        |
        +--> Rejects null elements (throws NullPointerException)
        +--> Rejects duplicate elements in Set/Map (throws IllegalArgumentException)
        +--> Disallows all mutators (throws UnsupportedOperationException)
        +--> Memory compaction (List0, List12, ListN)
```

### Detailed Implementation Mechanics

#### 1. Compact Internal Implementations (`List12` vs `ListN`)
Standard `ArrayList` allocates an `Object[]` buffer with default capacity 10, resulting in substantial pointer overhead. In contrast, `List.of()` uses specialized compact internal classes:
- `List0`: A static singleton representing the empty list (zero allocation).
- `List12`: Holds 1 or 2 elements in dedicated fields (`E e0; E e1;`) rather than an array, eliminating array object header overhead.
- `ListN`: Allocates a tightly sized array of exactly $N$ elements with zero excess capacity.

#### 2. Strict Null Rejection and Duplicate Detection
Modern factories enforce defensive preconditions:
- Passing `null` to `List.of()`, `Set.of()`, or `Map.of()` immediately throws `NullPointerException`.
- Passing duplicate elements to `Set.of("A", "A")` or duplicate keys to `Map.of("k", 1, "k", 2)` immediately throws `IllegalArgumentException` at compile-time/runtime.

#### 3. Defensive Copying with `copyOf()`
`List.copyOf(Collection<? extends E> coll)` inspects the runtime type of `coll`:
- If `coll` is already an unmodifiable collection created by `List.of()` or `List.copyOf()`, it simply returns `coll` directly without allocating a new object ($O(1)$ time and $O(1)$ space).
- If `coll` is any other mutable collection (e.g., `ArrayList`, `HashSet`), it iterates, validates non-nullity, and produces an independent compact immutable snapshot ($O(N)$ time).

questions.question: What happens when Set.of("apple", "banana", "apple") is executed at runtime?
options: It creates a Set with 2 unique elements: [apple, banana]
It throws IllegalArgumentException because Set.of strictly disallows duplicate elements
It compiles into a TreeSet that automatically deduplicates values
questions.explanation: Set.of() and Map.of() treat duplicate elements/keys as programming bugs and strictly throw IllegalArgumentException to enforce contract correctness at runtime.

questions.question: When List.copyOf(source) is invoked where 'source' is already an immutable list created by List.of(), what is the performance and memory behavior?
options: It allocates a new array and clones all references in O(N) time
It performs a deep clone of all stored objects
It returns 'source' directly in O(1) time with 0 additional heap allocation because source is already known to be structurally immutable
questions.explanation: List.copyOf(), Set.copyOf(), and Map.copyOf() recognize internal immutable collection classes and return the same reference immediately in O(1) time without redundant memory allocation.

questions.question: Which of the following allows elements to be replaced via set(int index, E element)?
questions.explanation: Arrays.asList() creates a fixed-size wrapper around an array. While it disallows structural additions or removals, it permits in-place element replacement via set(index, element).

activities.title: Principal Architect Interview Questions
activities.description: Deep-dive questions on defensive encapsulation, memory optimization, and concurrency safety.

questions.question: Why is Collections.unmodifiableList(list) insufficient for defensive encapsulation in multi-threaded systems?
questions.answer:
Collections.unmodifiableList creates a read-only decorator view over the existing list. It does not create an isolated copy. If another thread maintains a reference to the underlying mutable list and modifies it, the view immediately reflects those modifications.

Furthermore, if one thread iterates over the unmodifiable view while another thread mutates the backing list, a ConcurrentModificationException will be thrown. To achieve true defensive isolation and concurrent safety, systems must use List.copyOf() to create a detached, structurally immutable snapshot.

questions.question: How do List12 and ListN internal classes optimize memory consumption compared to traditional ArrayList?
questions.answer:
An ArrayList has object overhead plus an internal Object[] array reference with default capacity (10 slots), even if storing only 1 or 2 items. This creates two heap allocations and unused pointer slots.

In contrast, List.of() with 1 or 2 elements returns an instance of List12, which stores the references in direct instance fields (e0, e1) without allocating an array object at all. For 3 or more elements, ListN allocates an array with exact size matching the element count. This drastically reduces object overhead and garbage collection pressure in high-throughput services.

activities.title: Immutable Collections Mastery Checklist
activities.description: Verify your understanding of modern factory methods and defensive collection design.
items: I know that List.of(), Set.of(), and Map.of() immediately throw NullPointerException if any element or key/value is null.
I understand that Set.of() and Map.of() throw IllegalArgumentException on duplicate elements or duplicate keys.
I recognize that Arrays.asList() allows set(i, val) mutation which alters the underlying array.
I know that Collections.unmodifiableList() is a view and does not protect against mutations of the underlying backing collection.
I leverage List.copyOf() for true O(1) zero-allocation reuse when source is already an immutable collection.

practiceProblems.title: Safe Defensive Snapshot Factory
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `List<String> createSnapshot(List<String> source)` that returns an immutable list snapshot using `List.copyOf()`. If `source` is null, return an empty immutable list via `List.of()`.

practiceProblems.title: Null-Safe Immutable List Builder
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Because `List.of()` throws `NullPointerException` if any element is null, implement `List<String> safeImmutableList(String... items)` that filters out any null elements and returns an immutable list of the remaining elements using `List.copyOf()` or `List.of()`.

practiceProblems.title: Strict Deduplicated Immutable Set
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Because `Set.of()` throws `IllegalArgumentException` on duplicate items, implement `Set<String> safeImmutableSet(List<String> items)` that filters duplicates and nulls safely before converting to an immutable `Set` using `Set.copyOf()`.

practiceProblems.title: Immutable Configuration Map Builder
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `Map<String, String> buildConfig(List<String> keys, List<String> values)` that pairs corresponding non-null keys and non-null values into an immutable `Map`. If key and value list sizes differ, throw `IllegalArgumentException`. If duplicate keys exist, the last occurrence wins.

practiceProblems.title: Immutability Guard Validator
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `boolean isStructurallyImmutable(List<String> list)` that tests whether `list` rejects modifications by calling `list.add("test")` inside a try-catch block. If `UnsupportedOperationException` is caught, return `true`. Otherwise return `false`.
